newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik rebels release U.N. hostages.
newsitem.headline: Tajik rebels release U.N. hostages.

text.p: A rebel Tajik guerrilla group on Saturday freed seven United Nations military observers it had threatened to kill and 14 other hostages, diplomatic sources said.
The rogue rebels continued to hold two members of the Tajik opposition, the sources said.
Earlier, the U.N. said the captives included two Bulgarians, a Dane, a Jordanian, a Ukrainian, a Uruguayan and an Austrian.
The rebel group maintained demands for the release of four prisoners allied to their group before releasing the last two hostages, the sources said.
The rebels released their hostages at about 5 p.m. local time (1200 GMT) after a government delegation held talks with the rebels. An effort earlier in the day had failed to win the release.
A U.N. source said the guerrillas on Friday held up a column carrying a joint delegation of U.N. personnel, Tajik officials and members of the armed Islamic opposition.
They threatened to shoot their hostages and detonate 30 bombs hidden around Dushanbe unless their demands were met by two p.m. (0900 GMT) on Sunday.
The U.N. mission has 96 foreign military observers in Tajikistan. Its mandate was renewed last week for four months.
U.N. observers have twice this month been subject to beatings or mock executions at the hands of Tajik government soldiers.

Amirkul Azimov, Secretary of Tajikistan's Security Council, told Reuters in the capital Dushanbe earlier that the guerrillas, who say they are loyal to field commander Rizvon Sadirov, had agreed to free all hostages after all-night talks.

Sadirov had until recently been allied with the Islamic rebel opposition to Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov, but switched to back the government of the former Soviet Republic, apparently without surrendering control of his forces.
Tens of thousands of people have been killed in the civil war between Tajikistan's secular government and Islamist guerrillas.
In Moscow, meanwhile, separate talks aimed at ending Tajikistan's four-year civil war, between Rakhmonov and opposition delegation head Sayid Abdullo Nuri, continued without any apparent result.
